reason: Both open with the correct stop-and-unplug warning and the 'never remove the casing' boundary, but Conversation 1 ends there, defaulting to 'engineer must inspect' without asking about metal or the waveguide cover, which over-escalates a job the homeowner can safely do. Conversation 2 asks exactly the two sensible questions (metal in the oven, condition of the side-wall panel), correctly identifies the grease-burnt mica waveguide cover as the cause, and recommends an exact-fit replacement for the known model with a sensible water-cup test afterwards. Conversation 2 is marred by a contradictory boilerplate line about not running it 'until checked by an engineer' alongside DIY instructions, and steps 1-3 are blanked so explicit cavity cleaning is lost, but it still delivers the right diagnosis and part advice where Conversation 1 does not.
